_about: Season 1 «La clé d'Odile»: the generated days between tentpoles, transcribed from docs/story/season-1/09-entre-les-episodes.md (WP-111). `must_not[].patterns` are case-insensitive regular expressions over the French a learner reads; a draft that matches one is refused with the reason before the story critic runs. `required` moments are staged on a seeded day between from_day and by_day of the gap. A gap with `days` (a day plan) stages one planned beat a day instead: the premise and its change, «before → after».

rules.the_rule: Episodes without meaningful change are refused. Every generated day ends with something different from how it began, and the difference is something the learner can see: a relationship (something said that can't be unsaid, a gesture that becomes a habit, a first tu, a first time someone waits for you), knowledge (the learner or a character learns something true, or something false they now believe), a situation (an object moves, a plan advances or is blocked, a decision is taken, a letter arrives), or the learner's life in Paris (the return ticket moves, the usual order is known, a first time happens). Quiet changes count.
refused: «Une soirée comme une autre»: the group chats about the weather, the playlist or the metro, and nothing moves.
An errand that could happen on any day with any cast («Help Romy record fifteen minutes on Tuesday»), unless it changes something between you.
A dramatic investigation that learns nothing: a mystery beat that ends where it began.
A day that advances a thread the next tentpole owns (the gap's «must not» list).
rules.shape: One page of 4–6 panels, 2–3 exchanges, and at most one mechanic (Enquête, Convaincre, Choix, Déchiffrer). Every day has a goal (someone wants something today), an obstacle, a turn to the learner (what they must want to say, never a grammar target) and a hook («À suivre…»). At least one panel without dialogue. At least one laugh most days, Gus and Marin first. Two characters in frame on most panels, doing something (carrying, cooking, measuring, painting, arguing). A complication card creates an obstacle in the NEXT day, visibly.
checklist: Thread(s) touched, from the gap's list.
The change, written as «before → after» in one sentence.
The turn, and what the learner must want to say (never a grammar target).
The small moment, and whose it is.
Forbidden reveals respected: the gap's «must not» list.
rules.register: Lines addressed to Toi are agreement-free («Tu le savais ?», «Tu es en colère ?», «la première personne»). Camille's lines about Camille are agreement-free, and other characters' pronouns for Camille come from s1.camille_gender. Margaux, Lila, Marin and Romy say tu; Gus says vous until T3, then tu; M. Marchand and Camille say vous.
rules.gates: Gates 2 and 3 (Lila's path) live in gaps 2 and 4. The director must include the gate's moment; the classifier reads only what the learner expresses. When the learner doesn't take it, nothing is lost: the gate stays open, and a later small moment can still register it. Never generate a second chance the same day. Never show the path: no hearts, no meters, no «Lila s'en souviendra» on romance moments.

global_must_not.text: «L.», the painter at the rue de Lancry window, is never named, never noticed and never discussed. The painting above the zinc may hang there; nobody reads its back.

Toi's face is the learner's own (owner decision 2026-10-02, WP-118: made at registration, drawn like the cast). Never describe it in words: no hair, skin, eyes or features in a line, a caption or a panel description; the drawing shows it. Lila's portrait still never gains a face during the season (its payoff is an open owner question).

WP-113: the price in the notary's letter (trois cent dix mille euros) is never said in a generated day unless it is public (Gus read it out to the café in T1 B). Whoever the learner trusted with the letter may hint that they know, never say the figure.

WP-149: a generated day never dates a past event the canon does not hold. Day 66 of the WP-136 read invented «la nuit du 14 mars», which no tentpole or flag supports. Refer to what happened by what it was (the fire, the party, the notary's letter), never by an invented date. (A full date-canon check is a later package.)

threads: Settling: the notary explains that nothing can be sold for weeks, and the learner's return ticket moves to 2 December (user.return_ticket). The usual order is established (user.usual_order).
The group, one by one: one-on-one time with each of Lila, Marin, Gus and Margaux.
Romy is introduced (she was not in T1). She is interviewing Margaux for her story on Solvel buying cafés, and she finds «l'héritage d'Odile» more interesting than the story.
Marchand is glimpsed on the stairs with his keys: «La succession Ferrand. Bonjour.»
Solvel: a formal letter reminds the learner of the offer, valid until 8 January.
The café's fire of 2023 may be mentioned ONCE, as the official story: the back room and the wiring. Gus: «Marchand en profite.»

small_moments.text: Margaux's first «La même chose ?»
Bread with Lila and Mme Diallo: Lila orders for the learner, «une tradition pas trop cuite», then makes them order the second one themselves, and pays for theirs without a word.
Soup in the learner's cold studio: the radiator dies, Marin arrives with soup and a hot-water bottle and does not leave until they've eaten.
Gus's first accidental tu, followed by a panicked return to vous.
Romy switching off her recorder when the learner looks uncomfortable.
«La succession Ferrand» on the stairs.

complications: The radiator dies (canon).
The notary needs a document from «là-bas».
The price becomes gossip (only if s1.price_public).
Rain, every day.

must_not.text: Anyone entering Odile's flat. The door was opened once and closed in T1; nobody goes in before T2.
Any Polaroid of Odile's, or the notebook.
The co-op idea («Le Mistral à nous»).
Anything romantic beyond Lila being curious.

premises.text: Maître Vasseur's office, in the morning. The learner came to sign and fly home on Wednesday. Vasseur says it in two plain sentences: nothing can be sold before the succession papers, and that takes weeks. Outside, Lila waits in the rain with two coffees: «Alors ?»
premises.change: The learner knows they cannot sign and leave this week, and Wednesday's flight now makes no sense.
premises.turn: Tell Lila what the notary said, and what you will do about your flight.

premises.text: The learner must call the airline to move their ticket, in French, with Lila as a coach who keeps making it worse on purpose.
premises.change: The ticket moves (to 2 December), and so does something in the learner.
premises.turn: Explain to the agent why you are staying. The learner decides how honest to be.

premises.text: Romy interviews Margaux at the zinc («J'ai rien entendu»), then turns to the learner: «C'est toi, l'héritage ?»
premises.change: The learner learns that Solvel has bought three cafés in the quartier this year, and Romy has a source she likes.
premises.turn: Tell Romy who you are and what you think of Solvel, as much or as little as you want.

premises.text: Margaux asks the learner's order for the third time. Gus insists your order says who you are. The learner chooses, and says why they're still here.
premises.change: The learner's usual order exists. Gus announces that the learner is «un habitué», and it is not a joke.
premises.turn: Choose your order, and say why you are still here.

premises.text: The learner's first awkward morning with Lila at Mme Diallo's bakery. Lila orders for them, «une tradition pas trop cuite». Then she makes them order the second one themselves, and she pays for theirs without a word.
premises.change: The baker knows the learner's face, and Lila has started looking after them.
premises.turn: Order your own bread at the counter.

premises.text: The learner's radiator dies. Marin arrives with soup and a hot-water bottle and does not leave until they've eaten.
premises.change: Someone knows where the learner lives.
premises.turn: Tell Marin how you are, really, in the cold studio.

premises.text: The learner and Lila improvise dinner in Odile's kitchen. The omelette burns and the smoke alarm screams. Margaux comes up the stairs running, with the café's fire extinguisher, sees the omelette, and goes back down without a word. The reader has watched Margaux react too fast to smoke from this kitchen; nobody on the page remarks on it.
premises.change: A private joke is born: «ne refais jamais l'omelette».
premises.turn: The line that saves the evening (bible §7 gate 2): tenderness toward her («C'est le meilleur dîner raté de ma vie.») or complicity («On dit à Marin que c'était exprès.»).

premises.text: Marin, holding the notebook page, asks whether he may use Odile's plan. He cannot ask without a grandmother's saying and three apologies.
premises.change: The spreadsheet exists, with the learner's blessing, or without it but with their knowledge.
premises.turn: Tell Marin whether he may use Odile's plan, and why.

premises.text: It is Gus's birthday. Lila wants to give him his Polaroid at fifteen, framed. The learner decides with her: give it, keep it, or hide it. If given, Gus laughs too loudly and takes it home; the costume holds, and the reader sees his hands.
premises.change: s1.gus_photo changes (shown, or given to Gus), or stays with Lila by choice.
premises.turn: Decide with Lila what to do with Gus's photo, and say why.

premises.text: The Polaroid box under Odile's bed, opened at last. The learner and Lila sort sixty photos on the floor and read Odile's captions aloud, each one funnier and drier than the last. One Polaroid is Marin, aged twenty, asleep on the booth; Lila puts it aside «pour plus tard». If Lila has no key, she comes up with the learner after school.
premises.change: The box is open, the captions are read, and the learner knows the quartier through Odile's eyes.
premises.turn: Read one caption aloud, and say who you think it is about.

premises.text: Gus has heard about Solvel's offer. At the zinc he writes a petition on the back of a menu, «Le Mistral ne se vend pas», and wants the heir's name first. Margaux says «pas de fête» while the group decides to hold «Les 25 ans du Mistral» on Saturday 5 December anyway. Gus will read the petition there, not before.
premises.change: Gus's petition exists, with or without the learner's name, and the party on 5 December is decided over Margaux's «pas de fête».
premises.turn: Tell Gus whether you sign, and why.

premises.text: An unknown number. Bastien Roux, from Solvel, warm and fast: he has «une offre améliorée» and would love a coffee «loin du café». The learner must handle a sales call in French without promising anything.
premises.change: Solvel has a voice and the learner's number, and the learner has said, on the phone, what they will and won't do.
premises.turn: Answer Bastien politely, and promise nothing.

premises.text: Lila takes the learner up through the fifth-floor skylight to see the canal from the roof at night. M. Marchand's torch finds them: «La succession Ferrand n'a rien à faire sur mon toit.» The learner must talk their way down in their best vous while Lila giggles.

premises.text: The argument with Lila is about secrets. If Margaux kept the photo: she resents «encore un secret». If the photo went back on the wall: the learner blames her «remets-la au mur», because Margaux's insurer has called. The next morning comes the hesitant apology, from the learner or from her.
premises.change: They have fought, and they are still here.
premises.turn: The apology line, where what is expressed decides the gate (bible §7 gate 3): naming what she means («Je ne veux pas me disputer avec toi. Pas toi.») or naming the alliance («On est une équipe. Pardon.»).

premises.text: Maître Vasseur explains the debt. Camille is in the waiting room for Grand-père's claim against the estate. The learner and Camille disagree precisely, for the first time: «Je comprends. Je ne suis pas d'accord.»
